about: The answer to the one-line request of exercise 1, shown to participants as the starting point.
route: a Claude Code subagent given the request text as its whole prompt; the answer saved as returned
strengths: It apologises first for the one promise that was clearly broken: no delivery day was confirmed by Friday.
Its figures are right, and it does not promise the credit: it says it cannot approve the {money:creditAsked} itself, and that the {managerRole} will decide.
issues: It decides something nobody asked it to decide: "We will issue a corrected invoice that removes those cartons." No one in the thread offered that, and it is not what the policy says: missing goods are sent on the next delivery run (rule 2), so the cartons are still owed, not taken off the invoice.

It says "I have also sent her your receipt". Nothing in the thread says anyone has: in message 4, {staffFirst} sent the {managerRole} the photos and the request, and the receipt arrived only in message 5.
It promises an answer "the same day" to any further e-mail. The policy asks for one working day (rule 7); a same-day promise is one the writer may not be able to keep.

It promises a decision from the {managerRole} by a date: "Dana will give you her decision by [date, to be confirmed by Dana before sending]." The bracket asks for the date to be confirmed, but the promise that she will decide by then is made on her behalf.
It cannot be sent as it is: it has three gaps in square brackets, and formatting marks (the asterisks) that an e-mail program may show as they are.

Its own notes under the line are useful, and incomplete. They list the three gaps, and say that the thread does not show anyone agreeing to any part of the {money:creditAsked}. But they treat the corrected invoice as settled, asking only for its amount, and they say nothing about the receipt the reply says was sent. They also work out a date the thread does not give ("14 March"): right by the calendar, but worked out, so check it.
